key_insight: Interfaces between dissimilar 2D layers create out-of-plane dipoles that can be tuned by in-plane strain, enabling interface-engineered electromechanical responses.
engineering_relevance: Work-function mismatch and interfacial charge redistribution offer design handles for strain-tunable 2D electromechanical materials.
method: High-throughput DFT screening of 461 van der Waals heterostructures built from 57 monolayers.
Charge-density-difference analysis linking interfacial charge redistribution, dipoles, and biaxial strain.
Berry-phase validation of piezoelectric responses in semiconducting heterostructures.
evidence_signal: Across 24 selected heterostructures, effective biaxial interfacial electromechanical coefficients reach 83.35 pC/m; charge-density-difference and Berry-phase piezoelectric coefficients agree within 10% for semiconducting systems.
watch_item: The results are computational predictions; metallic-interface dipole tunability should not be conflated with well-defined semiconductor piezoelectricity.
paper_title: Interface-Engineered Piezoelectricity and Electromechanical Coupling in Two-Dimensional van der Waals Heterostructures
